extracted.intended_audience: HUD program participants, recipients, intermediaries, faith-based organizations, non-profit owners/operators, and Public Housing Agencies (PHAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for equal participation of faith-based organizations in HUD programs, beneficiary notice and nondiscrimination obligations, recordkeeping and audit rules, and disclosure/verification of Social Security and Employer Identification Numbers for applicants, participants, owners, and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-admission accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient, subrecipient, owner, operator, manager, or provider must take nondiscriminatory steps that may be necessary and appropriate to address privacy concerns raised by residents or occupants and, as needed, update its admissions, occupancy, and operating policies and procedures in accordance with paragraph (b) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to actions taken after admission to address privacy concerns; updates to admissions/occupancy/operating policies must be nondiscriminatory and follow paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and record retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers shall document and maintain records of compliance with the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section for a period of 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records evidencing compliance for five years; applies to providers subject to the cited paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirements for non-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-profit organizations subject to regulations in the part 200 and part 800 series of title 24 of the CFR shall comply with the audit requirements of 2 CFR part 200, subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For HUD programs, a non-profit organization is the mortgagor or owner (as defined in parts 200 and 800) and not a related or affiliated organization; follow federal audit rules in 2 CFR part 200 subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal participation — general eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith-based organizations are eligible, on the same basis as any other organization, to participate in any HUD program or activity for which they are otherwise eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither HUD nor entities administering HUD programs shall discriminate for or against an organization on the basis of the organization's religious character, motives, affiliation, or lack thereof, or on the basis of conduct that would not be grounds to favor/disfavor a similarly situated secular organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case accommodations for religious exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section shall be construed to preclude HUD from making an accommodation, including for religious exercise, with respect to one or more program requirements on a case-by-case basis in accordance with the Constitution and laws of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accommodations may be granted consistent with applicable constitutional and statutory law; handled individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-disqualification for expressing intent to request an accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD shall not disqualify an organization from participating in any HUD program for which it is eligible on the basis of the organization's indication that it may request an accommodation, unless the organization has made clear that the accommodation is necessary to its participation and HUD has determined that it would deny the accommodation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely indicating potential accommodation needs cannot be the basis for disqualification; disqualification only if accommodation is clearly necessary and HUD legitimately denies it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards decisions must be merit-based and politically neutral
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions about awards of Federal financial assistance must be free from political interference or the appearance of such interference and must be made on the basis of merit, not based on the organization's religious character, affiliation, or religious exercise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of funding opportunity, grant agreements, and cooperative agreements shall include language substantially similar to Appendix A affirming eligibility of faith-based organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and identity of faith-based organizations (use of funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: A faith-based organization that applies for or participates in a HUD program supported with Federal financial assistance retains its autonomy, right of expression, religious character, authority over its governance, and independence, and may continue to carry out its mission; provided that it does not use direct Federal financial assistance to support or engage in any explicitly religious activities (e.g., worship, religious instruction, proselytization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct Federal funds cannot support explicitly religious activities, but the organization otherwise retains autonomy and religious expression in governance and mission documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious symbols and governance retention
rubrics_metrics.description: A faith-based organization that receives direct Federal financial assistance may use space in its facilities to carry out HUD-funded activities without concealing, altering, or removing religious art, icons, scriptures, or other religious symbols, and may retain religious terms in its name and select board members on the basis of adherence to religious tenets consistent with paragraph (i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Religious identity and symbols may remain; selection of governance consistent with applicable nondiscrimination and employment-exemption rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of explicitly religious activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an organization engages in explicitly religious activities (including worship, religious instruction, or proselytization), the explicitly religious activities must be offered separately, in time or location, from the programs or activities supported by direct Federal financial assistance and participation must be voluntary for beneficiaries of programs that receive direct Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies to direct federal assistance; indirect federal assistance is not subject to this restriction. HUD retains authority to fund activities consistent with the Establishment Clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediary responsibilities for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: If an intermediary is given authority to select a nongovernmental organization to receive Federal financial assistance under an agreement, the intermediary must ensure that such organization complies with the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediaries distributing HUD funds must enforce the same rules; nongovernmental intermediaries otherwise retain their program rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination toward beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organization that receives Federal financial assistance under a HUD program shall not, in providing services supported in whole or in part with Federal financial assistance, or in outreach activities related to such services, discriminate against a beneficiary or prospective beneficiary on the basis of religion, a religious belief, a refusal to hold a religious belief, or a refusal to attend or participate in a religious practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations funded by indirect assistance need not modify their programs to accommodate a beneficiary who chooses to expend the indirect aid on the organization's program; discrimination prohibition applies to services funded by federal assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary written notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization providing services under a program supported by direct Federal financial assistance from HUD, or an entity that administers indirect Federal financial assistance from HUD, must give written notice to beneficiaries and prospective beneficiaries of certain protections in a manner and form prescribed by HUD, including by incorporating the notice into materials that are otherwise provided to beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required language for this written notice is set forth in Appendix C to this subpart; notices must be provided in HUD-prescribed manner and form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific notice responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: For HCV, PBV, and Section 8 Moderate Rehabilitation programs the Public Housing Agency is required to provide the written beneficiary notice; for HOPWA, the grantee or project sponsor responsible for eligibility determinations must provide the notice; for CoC and ESG programs, the recipient or subrecipient responsible for determining eligibility is required to provide the notice. Participating or prospective providers (landlords) are not responsible for providing the written beneficiary notice for indirect aid recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities differ by program—recipient/subrecipient/grantee roles specified explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of beneficiary notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must include (A) the nondiscrimination requirements of paragraph (g)(1); (B) notification that a beneficiary or prospective beneficiary may report an organization's violation of these protections and how to file a complaint; and (C) for direct Federal financial assistance only, prohibitions with respect to explicitly religious activities as set forth in paragraph (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C contains model language and contact information (e.g., HUD's Center for Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships) for reporting violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of beneficiary notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The written notice must be given to a prospective beneficiary prior to the time the prospective beneficiary enrolls in the program or receives services from the program. When it is impracticable due to the nature of the service or exigent circumstances, an organization must advise beneficiaries of their protections at the earliest available opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice is required except in exigent circumstances; if delayed, provide at earliest possible time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative option information in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD may determine that the notice must inform each beneficiary or prospective beneficiary about how to obtain information from HUD, or a State agency or other entity administering the applicable program, about other federally funded service providers in their area that provide the services available under the applicable program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices may be required to include referrals or information about alternative federally funded providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on additional assurances from faith-based organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: No notice of funding opportunity, grant agreement, cooperative agreement, covenant, memorandum of understanding, policy, or regulation used by HUD or a recipient or intermediary shall require otherwise eligible faith-based organizations to provide assurances or notices where they are not required of similarly situated secular organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faith-based organizations should not face additional eligibility conditions beyond those imposed on secular counterparts; must still comply with general program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of Title VII religious employment exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: A religious organization's exemption from the Federal prohibition on employment discrimination on the basis of religion, set forth in section 702(a) of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, is not forfeited when the organization participates in a HUD program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some HUD programs may impose independent nondiscrimination requirements; grantees should consult the HUD program office to determine scope of applicable requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on use of direct Federal funds for acquisition/construction/rehabilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Federal financial assistance may be used for acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation of structures only to the extent that those structures are used for conducting eligible activities under a HUD program. Where a structure is used for both eligible and explicitly religious activities, direct Federal assistance may not exceed the cost of the share attributable to eligible activities. Acquisition, construction, or rehabilitation of sanctuaries, chapels, or other rooms that a HUD-funded faith-based organization uses as its principal place of worship may not be paid with direct Federal financial assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost accounting must reflect the share attributable to eligible (secular) activities; disposition and change-in-use rules follow government-wide real property disposition regs (2 CFR part 200, subpart D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commingling of Federal and State/tribal/local funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State, tribal, or local government voluntarily contributes its own funds to supplement direct Federal financial assistance for an activity, the State, tribal or local government has the option to segregate those funds or commingle them with the direct Federal financial assistance. However, if the funds are commingled, the requirements of this section apply to all of the commingled funds. Matching funds required by statute are considered commingled and subject to the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commingled funds inherit the federal restrictions; consult program office where program-specific rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax-exempt / nonprofit eligibility evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD does not generally require that recipients obtain 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status to be eligible for funding, but many grant programs require nonprofit status and will state that requirement. Where nonprofit status must be shown but is not statutorily defined, applicants may demonstrate nonprofit status by: (1) IRS recognition under 501(c)(3); (2) statement from a State taxing body certifying nonprofit status and that no part of net earnings benefits private individuals; (3) certified copy of certificate of incorporation; or (4) applicable parent-organization documentation plus a statement that the applicant is a local affiliate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFAs will specify eligibility requirements; applicants should consult appropriate HUD program office for program-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of construction regarding religions
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither HUD nor any recipient or intermediary receiving funds under any HUD program shall construe these provisions in such a way as to advantage or disadvantage faith-based organizations affiliated with historic or well-established religions or sects in comparison with other religions or sects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation must be neutral across religions and sects; avoid preferential or adverse treatment of historic vs. other religions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A — NOFO model language for faith-based applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFOs should state that faith-based organizations may apply on the same basis as any other organization, HUD will not discriminate on account of religious character, and faith-based organizations retain independence but may not use direct HUD funds for explicitly religious activities and may not discriminate in providing HUD-funded services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A provides model wording to be included in Notices of Funding Opportunity to ensure consistent treatment of faith-based applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B — Notice of Award/Contract model language
rubrics_metrics.description: A faith-based organization that participates in the program retains independence and may not use direct Federal financial assistance to support explicitly religious activities; organization receiving funds may not discriminate in providing HUD-funded services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B provides model wording for award or contract documents to reflect these principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C — Model written beneficiary notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: Model notice must state: (1) the program may not discriminate on basis of religion or refusal to hold beliefs; (2) the organization may not require attendance at explicitly religious activities and participation must be voluntary; (3) separation in time/location of privately funded explicitly religious activities from HUD-funded activities; (4) how to report violations (HUD Center for Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnership contact information); and (5) how to obtain information about other federally funded providers in the area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model notice must be given before enrollment or receipt of services unless impracticable; Appendix C provides model text and contact info (including partnerships@hud.gov and mailing address).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of SSN/EIN disclosure and verification (Subpart B)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart B requires applicants and participants in covered HUD programs to disclose, and submit documentation to verify, their Social Security Numbers (SSNs). It also enables HUD and PHAs to obtain income information through computer matches with SWICAs and Federal agencies, and from financial institutions and employers, to verify eligibility or level of assistance. The purpose is to enable HUD to decrease the incidence of fraud, waste, and abuse in the covered programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSN disclosure is for eligibility verification and anti-fraud; tied to computer matching and income verification processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of SSN/EIN disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart B applies to mortgage and loan insurance and coinsurance and housing assistance programs contained in chapter II, subchapter B, and chapters VIII and IX of this title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check program chapter/part applicability; not necessarily universal across all HUD programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of information covered by consent forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Information covered by consent forms described in this subpart involves income information from SWICAs, wages, income, and resource information from financial institutions, net earnings from self-employment, payments of retirement income, and unearned income as referenced at 26 U.S.C. 6103. Consent forms may authorize collection of other information necessary to determine eligibility or level of benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent forms expire after a certain time; may cover IRS return information and other income sources per cited statutes and program regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal preemption of inconsistent State law (Subpart B)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart B preempts any State law, including restrictions and penalties, that governs the collection and use of income information to the extent State law is inconsistent with this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal disclosure/verification rules supersede conflicting state statutes or penalties for collection/use of income information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the Privacy Act and other law
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of SSNs, EINs, any information derived from SSNs and EINs, and income information under this subpart shall be conducted, to the extent applicable, in compliance with the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. 552a) and all other provisions of Federal, State, and local law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy Act obligations apply; ensure appropriate notices and safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act notice timing
rubrics_metrics.description: All assistance applicants shall be provided with a Privacy Act notice at the time of application. All participants shall be provided with a Privacy Act notice at each annual income recertification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required Privacy Act notice at application and annually for participants during recertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined terms relevant to disclosure and participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions that govern the Subpart include: Assistance applicant; Computer match; Computer matching agreement; Consent form; Employer Identification Number (EIN); Entity applicant; Federal agency; Income information; Individual owner applicant; IRS; Owner; Participant; Processing entity; Social Security Number (SSN); SSA; State Wage Information Collection Agency (SWICA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions specify who must disclose, what data may be obtained, and roles (e.g., processing entity = person/entity responsible for eligibility determinations). See §5.214 for full definitions and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of assistance applicants (§5.216(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each assistance applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to the assistance applicant and to each member of the assistance applicant's household, and the documentation referred to in paragraph (g)(1) of this section to verify each such SSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure and verification occur when the assistance applicant's eligibility under the program involved is being determined; paragraph (g)(1) (not fully shown here) defines acceptable documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of individual owner applicants (§5.216(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual owner applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to the individual owner applicant and to each member of the individual owner applicant's household who will be obligated to pay the debt evidenced by the mortgage or loan documents, and the documentation referred to in paragraph (g)(1) to verify each such SSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies at the time the individual owner applicant's eligibility under the program is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of certain officials of entity applicants (§5.216(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each officer, director, principal stockholder, or other official of an entity applicant must submit the complete and accurate SSN assigned to each such individual and the documentation referred to in paragraph (g)(1) to verify each SSN when the entity applicant's eligibility is being determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets key officials of entity applicants (partnerships, corporations, etc.) when determining eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure required of participants — initial disclosure conditions (§5.216(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant, except those age 62 or older as of January 31, 2010, whose initial determination of eligibility was begun before January 31, 2010, must submit required SSN information if the participant has not previously disclosed an SSN, previously disclosed a SSN that HUD or the SSA determined was invalid, or (additional conditions continue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial disclosure obligations depend on participant age, previous disclosures, and SSA/HUD validation; further conditions are specified in the remainder of the section.
